'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Afghanistan conflict (1978–present)|Afghanistan conflict]]
**[[Islamic State–Taliban conflict]]
***[[2021 Kabul hospital attack]]
****A [[improvised explosive device|bomb]] explodes at the entrance of the [[Daoud Khan Military Hospital]] in [[Kabul]], followed by gunfire and a second explosion. At least 25 people are killed and more than 50 others are wounded. Four of the attackers are killed and a fifth is arrested by the [[Taliban]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/nov/02/deadly-explosions-hit-military-hospital-in-kabul-afghanistan (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Insurgency in the Maghreb (2002–present)|Insurgency in the Maghreb]]
**[[2021 Niger attacks]]
***At least 69 people are killed as [[Islamic State in the Greater Sahara]] gunmen attack a delegation led by the mayor of [[Banibangou]], in [[Niger]]. The mayor is among those killed. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/11/4/dozens-dead-in-west-niger-village-attack-officials (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Tigray War]]
**Ethiopia declares a six-month [[state of emergency]] as the [[Tigray Defense Forces]] (TDF) and [[Oromo Liberation Army]] gain control over areas outside of [[Tigray Region|Tigray]] and the TDF announces its intention to advance to the Ethiopian capital, [[Addis Ababa]]. Authorities in Addis Ababa, in a separate announcement earlier in the day, tell citizens to register arms and prepare to defend their neighbourhoods. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/addis-ababa-government-urges-residents-register-arms-media-2021-11-02/ (Reuters)]
**The [[United States]] bans [[embassy]] personnel from traveling outside of Addis Ababa and strongly suggests that U.S. citizens seriously reconsider travel to Ethiopia and that those who are currently in Ethiopia consider making preparations to leave the country. [https://et.usembassy.gov/security-alert-update-on-security-situation-in-ethiopia/ (U.S. Embassy in Ethiopia)]

'''Business and economy'''
*The Taliban announces a [[Taliban foreign currency ban|complete ban on the use of foreign currency]] in transactions, threatening "legal action" against those who defy the ban. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/11/2/taliban-bans-use-of-foreign-currency-across-afghanistan (Al Jazeera)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*Five people are dead after a small [[Cargo aircraft|cargo plane]] belonging to Optimum Aviation Ltd. crashes shortly after take-off from [[Juba International Airport|the airport]] in [[Juba]], [[South Sudan]]. [https://apnews.com/article/business-africa-south-sudan-juba-plane-crashes-5ccb8559b02c6d143090dc281f3f4cea (AP)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Bulgaria]]
****[[Bulgaria]] reports a record 6,007 new cases and 310 [[COVID-19 pandemic deaths|deaths]] from [[COVID-19]] in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 608,499 and the nationwide death toll to 24,309. [https://www.novinite.com/articles/212093/COVID-19+in+Bulgaria%3A+6007+New+Cases%2C+310+Deaths%2C+14%2C545+Newly+Vaccinated+in+Last+24h (''Novinite'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Greece]]
****[[Greece]] reports a record 6,700 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours,  bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 754,451. [https://www.ekathimerini.com/news/1170980/greece-logs-record-high-daily-covid-19-infections/amp/ (''Ekathimerini'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Romania]]
****[[Romania]] reports a record 591 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 48,664. [https://www.reuters.com/article/health-coronavirus-romania/romanias-covid-19-deaths-at-new-record-high-idINL8N2R21X4 (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
****[[Russia]] reports a record 1,178 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 240,871. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/latest-on-coronavirus-outbreak/russia-hits-another-grim-record-of-daily-coronavirus-deaths/2409725 (Anadolu Agency)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Tonga]]
****[[Tonga]]'s main island of [[Tongatapu]] enters a seven-day [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] that closes non-essential businesses and bans sales of alcohol and mass gatherings, except small funerals, after the country reports its first case of COVID-19 in a person who travelled from [[Christchurch]], [[New Zealand]] on a [[repatriation]] flight last week. [https://www.nzherald.co.nz/world/covid-19-delta-outbreak-tongas-main-island-going-into-lockdown/HLQAK6ZZAKWYQOMOYOPXTCBYIQ/ (''New Zealand Herald'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Tuvalu]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand]]
****A traveller from [[Tuvalu]] tests positive for COVID-19 upon arrival in [[Auckland]], [[New Zealand]]. Tuvalu had not previously reported any COVID-19 cases in the country. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/454774/traveller-from-tuvalu-tests-positive-for-covid-19-in-nz (RNZ)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Argentina]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Argentina]]
***[[Argentina]] begins administering [[booster dose]]s of the [[COVID-19 vaccine]] for people over the age of 50 years old and people with [[Autoimmune disease|immunization problems]]. [https://www.infobae.com/salud/2021/11/02/terceras-dosis-de-vacunas-covid-en-la-argentina-quienes-las-reciben-y-que-vacunas-se-usan/ (''Infobae'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Bahrain]]
***[[Bahrain]]'s [[National Health Regulatory Authority (Bahrain)|National Health Regulatory Authority]] approves the emergency use of the [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine]] for children between the ages of 5 and 11 years old. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/bahrain-gives-emergency-approval-to-pfizer-coronavirus-shots-for-kids-5-11/ (''The Times of Israel'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 vaccination in the United States]]
****The [[Centers for Disease Control and Prevention|U.S. CDC]] approves the [[Pfizer]]–[[BioNTech]] COVID-19 vaccine for children aged 5 and 11 years old. [https://variety.com/2021/politics/news/cdc-covid19-vaccine-children-5-to-11-1235103409/ (''Variety'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[Foreign relations of Madagascar]], [[Foreign relations of Seychelles]]
**[[Seychelles]] [[President of the Seychelles|president]] [[Wavel Ramkalawan]] and Malagasy president [[Andry Rajoelina]] hold a bilateral meeting in [[Glasgow]] to discuss [[trafficking]] in the south of Seychelles and [[maritime security]] in the [[Indian Ocean]]. The two leaders also discuss ways to stop gold smuggling. [https://allafrica.com/stories/202111020261.html (AllAfrica)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2021 United States elections]]
**[[2021 United States gubernatorial elections]]
***[[2021 Virginia gubernatorial election]], [[2021 New Jersey gubernatorial election]]
****Voters head to the polls in [[Virginia]] to either re-elect former [[Governor of Virginia|Governor]] [[Terry McAuliffe]] or elect former [[The Carlyle Group|Carlyle Group]] [[Chief executive officer|CEO]] [[Glenn Youngkin]]. In [[New Jersey]], voters head to the polls to either re-elect [[Governor of New Jersey|Governor]] [[Phil Murphy]] or elect former state legislator [[Jack Ciattarelli]] to replace him. [https://www.kitv.com/story/45103683/here-are-the-major-2021-races-to-watch (KITV-TV)]
****Youngkin defeats McAuliffe, making him the first [[Republican Party of Virginia|Virginia Republican]] to win a [[2009 Virginia gubernatorial election|statewide race]] since [[Bob McDonnell]] in 2009. [[Winsome Sears]] will become the first woman of color to be elected [[Lieutenant Governor of Virginia]]. [https://apnews.com/article/ap-news-alert-virginia-18bc0c626446eed03099adab52c2c544 (AP)] [https://www.washingtonpost.com/local/virginia-politics/virginia-lieutenant-governor/2021/11/02/27f9ed8c-36b3-11ec-91dc-551d44733e2d_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]
**[[2021 United States House of Representatives elections]]
***[[2021 Ohio's 15th congressional district special election]], [[2021 Ohio's 11th congressional district special election]]
****Voters head to the polls to replace [[Steve Stivers]] and [[Marcia Fudge]]. Fudge resigned in March in order to become [[United States Secretary of Housing and Urban Development|U.S. Secretary of Housing and Urban Development]]. [https://www.bignewsnetwork.com/news/271624622/ohio-residents-urged-to-vote-in-tuesday-general-election (Big News Network)]
*[[2021 Maine referendums]]
**[[Maine]] voters approve three questions on ballot in 2021, which ban the construction of [[Hydro Québec]]'s high-voltage line to [[Massachusetts]] that passes through the state, authorize issuing $100 million in infrastructure bonds and amend the [[Constitution of Maine]] to declare a right to produce and consume food of their choice for personal usage. [https://bangordailynews.com/elections-central/ (''Bangor Daily News'')]
*[[Christian Schmidt (politician)|Christian Schmidt]], the [[United Nations]]' [[High Representative for Bosnia and Herzegovina]], issues a report warning that the country is likely to break apart and that there is a very high risk of the renewal of internal [[armed conflict]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/nov/02/bosnia-is-in-danger-of-breaking-up-warns-eus-top-official-in-the-state (''The Guardian'')]

'''Sports'''
*In [[Major League Baseball]], the [[Atlanta Braves]] defeat the [[Houston Astros]] to win the [[2021 World Series|World Series]]. This marks the Braves' first World Series title since [[1995 World Series|1995]].
